title: Nigerian Spiced Peanut Beef Skewers
summary: Thin slices of beef are coated in a dry, peanut-spiced yaji rub and grilled hot and fast for smoky, charred skewers, served with crunchy raw vegetables and lime.
equipment: 8-12 metal skewers (or wooden skewers soaked 30 min)
barbecue or ridged cast-iron griddle pan

ingredients.note: up to 1 tsp for more heat

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
small red onion, thinly sliced into rings

steps.title: Blend the yaji spice
steps.text: Blitz the peanuts, ginger, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, cayenne, white pepper and salt in a food processor for 20-30 seconds in short bursts, until finely ground but not pasty. Watch the texture closely; over-processing releases the peanuts' oil and turns the mix into peanut butter instead of a dry spice rub. Set a third of the yaji aside in a separate bowl for serving later.

steps.title: Slice the beef thin
steps.text: Freeze the beef for 20 minutes until firm, then slice it against the grain into pieces about 5mm thick. Firming the meat first makes it much easier to cut thin, even slices, which is what lets the yaji coat every surface and the beef cook quickly on the grill.

steps.title: Marinate the beef
steps.text: Toss the sliced beef with the remaining yaji, the oil and the beef salt until every piece is well coated. Cover and refrigerate for anywhere from 30 minutes up to 12 hours; the longer rest lets the spice and salt season the meat right through.

steps.title: Skewer and prep onion
steps.text: Weave 2-3 slices of beef onto each skewer, pressing them flat so the meat cooks at an even rate. Rinse the sliced onion rings in cold water and pat them dry, which softens their raw bite ready for serving alongside the hot skewers.

steps.title: Grill until charred
steps.text: Heat a barbecue or ridged griddle pan over high heat until very hot, then grill the skewers for 2-4 minutes a side until browned and crisp at the edges and cooked through, with the thickest piece reading 63°C on a probe thermometer. High heat sears the thin slices quickly, giving the characteristic charred edge before the inside overcooks. Rest under foil for 3 minutes, then sprinkle with 1 tablespoon of the reserved yaji for a fresh hit of spice.

steps.title: Serve with salad
steps.text: Serve the skewers with the sliced onion, tomato, shredded cabbage, cucumber and lime wedges, along with the rest of the reserved yaji on the side for dipping. The crunchy raw vegetables and sharp lime cut through the richness of the spiced beef.

tips: Freezing the beef briefly before slicing makes thin, even cuts much easier to achieve.
A common mistake is over-blending the yaji until it turns oily; pulse in short bursts and stop once it's finely ground.
Marinate for as long as you can spare - even a few hours deepens the flavour, but overnight is even better.
Keep the grill or griddle very hot so the beef chars quickly without drying out.
Save some yaji to sprinkle on just before serving for an extra layer of spice.
storage: Cool any leftovers within 2 hours, refrigerate for up to 2 days, and reheat in a hot pan or under the grill until piping hot (74°C) before eating.
